title: Mentorship and Peer Review in Biomedical AI
audience: Clinical learners practicing mentorship communication in clinical AI teams
objectives: Identify communication, expectation, workload, and career-dynamic problems in clinical AI mentorship.
Draft a professional message that balances urgency, respect, and independence.
Reflect on mentorship challenges specific to clinical AI and clinical research teams.

sections.name: Clinical Case
sections.purpose: Introduce a strained mentorship relationship around workflow integration, protocol deadlines, and IRB submission.
sections.how_to_use: Read the case and notice both Dr. Jordan's support needs and Dr. Martinez's concern about independence.

sections.name: Identify the Challenges
sections.purpose: Separate communication breakdown, expectation mismatch, workload conflict, and career-stage dynamics.
sections.how_to_use: Write bullet points describing the clinical mentoring problems, then optionally compare with the example.

sections.name: Draft a Professional Communication
sections.purpose: Practice respectful, concrete communication for busy clinical environments.
sections.how_to_use: Draft a message that requests a meeting, acknowledges clinical workload, and proposes structured check-ins or agendas.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Apply the scenario to clinical AI teams.
sections.how_to_use: Write what makes clinical AI mentorship hard and how these techniques could help in your own team.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through reading the clinical case, identifying challenges, drafting the message, and reflecting.
For clinical users, emphasize busy schedules, hierarchy, urgent deadlines, patient-care workload, and structured check-ins.
Help learners write messages that are direct, respectful, and actionable.
